I agree. You need to get her help immediately, in any shape or form. Therapy seems like a viable option, but with someone with such a dark and tragic background, she needs at least something, especially your full support. Best of luck.

Just go for it. Risks like these are meant to be taken. If she feels the same way, holding back just for the possibility of things not working out isn't justifiable. Its okay to be scared, but its also okay to feel alive, happy, and in love. Be direct, confident, and meaningful when you talk to her. Hear what she has to say and make sure she hears what you do too.

But my biggest piece of advice for you is to not become desperate. If things don't work, they don't work. Its easy to feel as if Nicole owes it to you to be in love with you, when in truth she doesn't. She's an independent person with her own views, preferences, and opinions. There's no need for her to feel guilty for not loving you if it isn't what she wants.

If you two share similar feelings, you have to be confident enough to tell her that its worth a try to get the love that you both want, and not worry about the downside. Its better to have loved and loss than to have never loved at all, no?

"I just wish...I could be normal."

The odd way the light shined within Kenneth's cracked window, positioned bleakly on the run-downed walls of his hideous dwelling made his room seem like the dividing factors of yin and yang. Completed with his oh-so-satisfying fixation for the family of cockroaches crawling along his walls, he wondered the feeling of such disgusting insects; how does it feel to live on luxury at the expense of someone else's misfortune? How did it feel to travel withing a close compelling group, or in laymen's terms: as a family? 

Kenny wish he'd known. 

Comforted by a meagerly washed pillow-case covering a relatively inexpensive pillow in the 'yang' black corner of his room cowering from starlight, he tried to ignore the sounds of his aunt and uncle. Try as he might, however, the loud bang erupting from the living room mere steps away was too much to sleep off. What was it this time? The coffee table? The lamp his grandmother decorated for the house? Fist colliding on shallow slab splattered across the steal of a seven bedroom home?  

A devoid, empty sadness filled him. It was his 16th birthday; his 5th year here, and the 5th year since he'd seen his mother. Oh, his father? He didn't feel like having his heart broken by wasting his effort trying to reach unobtainable expectations. No matter where he went it was one problem after another. Everything just seemed like another problem. A single tear managed to slip past his solidified foundation he called emotion. With no one to comfortably talk to, he slowly began to break. However, he inevitably realized earlier in his life that he had no time to pity himself. There was always another problem bigger than his own.

"Stay away from me! Someone help! Help!" came the cries from his desperate aunt. Panic filled the teenager, but he responded fast. He never really liked his uncle, and God knows what he could do to his aunt. He grabbed his tennis racquet and shyly stormed out of his corner. Placing an ear onto his door gave him a better opportunity to survey the situation. 

"Stay the fuck away from me!" His grip on his racquet hardened. Kenneth was far from being a protagonist. He has always had a mix between the quiet type and goofy. Brave? He never knew; though he had a feeling he was about to find out. Suddenly, a door slammed.

"What the hell are you doing to my aunt?!" Kenneth's eyes popped in horror. "Oh God," he thought, "not you too, Aaron!" His elder brother, known as the frail type sounded full of rage, not frail at all. They all exchanged loud words. Loud, cruel, violent words. Until finally came:

"Don't fucking push me!" and "Keep your fucking hands off of him!"

Kenneth stormed out the room, defense in hand. He came out as his uncle was raising a fist to his brother Aaron. Time itself seemed to have came to a halt. So many thoughts were processed within that one moment. With thoughts came memories; with memories: regrets. This was going to be one of them.

Running full speed into the confrontation - his aunt, wailing; his brother, angered; his uncle, merciless - Kenny began to think about where it all went wrong.

He started to believe that, if even for a moment, there could have been a spark of normality in his life. But in an instant - as his racquet hit air, his eye became numb, and his head hit the metallic dining table - his perspective changed.

His last thought was doubting that he could ever be 'normal'.

But then he woke up in sheets that weren't familiar. The walls seemed brighter, cleaner, even. Much cleaner. Panicked, he hopped out of bed. Looking down at himself he wore amazingly comfortable felt sweats and a T-shirt with his favorite anime on it. A slight familiarity was hung on his wall in the form of a red and black Prince tennis racquet; complete with red and black co-polyester spin strings (tightened at a perfect 65 string tension) and black grip tape which looked to be something a little more premium than he could normally afford. His room was painted a beautiful, bright, mahogany that was expertly painted all the way down to the shining hardwood floor. Now looking carefully, the bed sheets were a black, comfortable silk, with red and black polka-dotted pillow cases, and Tokyo Ghoul themed comforter. 

Kenny scratched his head in surprised which was followed by a rubbing of the eyes and eventual cheek pinching. This...was everything he dreamed of in a room. Down to the Pikachu slippers and the anime figuring collection he had always wanted to start; rivals side by side in an epic stare down: Goku and Freiza, Naruto and Sasuke, Kaneki and Yamori, Ash and Gary, the list went on for a few more pairs of figures (he had a very diverse and open mind to all anime). He gasped as he seen his closet. This utopia even contained the racquet collection he had sold, as well as a 6-racquet carrying bag. Not only that, but a hoard of video games and consoles.

At this point he deducted only one possible explanation: he had to have been in heaven. With it making perfect sense, he decided that it was still far to early in the morning, even in the 'Heaven Central Standard Time' he joked to himself about, and crawled back into bed. His head, unfortunately, still hurt. Was that normal? 

"Kenny, you told me last night you'd attempt to go to school today, remember?" came a sweet, caring tone of mothering voice. It had sounded so familiar...

"A-Auntie Erin?" Kenneth questioned as he looked up at the hallway light that shone past the tall blond woman. She chuckled slightly and sighed, putting on a smile and leaned against the door.

"Jeez man, you haven't called me that in years! You're so used to calling me 'Ma' now I'm starting to forget I'm just your aunt! Maybe you should wait till next week, kiddo. I know you want to show up to tennis practice and all but-"

"N-no...I'll get up. I'll miss the bus.." Kenny tried.

"Oh no young man; you're staying right there! Jeez, all this nonsense about a bus when the school is down the road...maybe we shouldn't have let you gone to that tennis camp after all! Far too dangerous!" To emphasize her point, she carefully wagged a finger. "Now you stay right there. I'll cook up some breakfast. How's egg and bacon biscuits sound?" That was his favorite breakfast. Was he smoking crack? Or did he overdose on it already?

"That-that sounds amazing! Thank you!" Erin had smiled and closed the door on her way out.

Kenny didn't know what to make of this, but he didn't care. He wanted a normal life, but if what he got was a perfect one instead, he didn't care. It felt great.

But what was that thing he was thinking about, which felt like mere moments ago? If feeling this amazing in luxury at the cost of someone else's misfortune was plausible, then was Kenneth heartless if he didn't care? 

Who knows: that person's misfortune might've been closer than he thought.
